verdict_reason: RFC 9457 member set is correct and matches the runtime ProblemDetail body, but the record diverges from docs/openapi/api-contract.locked.yaml on traceId vs trace_id and, lacking any @Schema annotations, drops the contract's required list, descriptions and examples from the generated spec.

todos.issue: The record's traceId member contradicts docs/openapi/api-contract.locked.yaml, which declares Problem.trace_id in snake_case and documents it as 'a deliberate divergence from the animals-backend's camelCase traceId' — the exact opposite of this Javadoc's cv-001 rationale; OperatorComplianceIT's divergence gate only compares path sets and operationIds, so the drift passes CI unnoticed.
todos.fix: Pick one source of truth and make the other follow: if cv-001 camelCase stands (as the IT and generated operators.yml assert), update the locked contract's Problem/ValidationProblem schemas to traceId and drop the snake_case rationale text; otherwise rename the record member. Consider extending the IT's divergence gate to compare component schema property names, not just paths and operationIds.

todos.issue: The record carries no @Schema annotations, so the generated docs/openapi/operators.yml Problem schema has no description, no examples and — critically — no required list, while the locked contract declares required: [type, title, status]; every 400/404/500 response in the published contract therefore advertises all five members as optional to generated clients.
todos.fix: Annotate the record type with @Schema(description = "RFC 9457 problem details") and each component with @Schema(description = ..., example = ...), adding requiredMode = Schema.RequiredMode.REQUIRED on type, title and status (leave detail and traceId optional). Apply the same to ValidationProblem so its errors member is marked required as the contract's allOf branch requires.
